exercises.prompt: Complete: *Me alegra mucho que tú ___ a la boda.* (venir)

options.label: vengas
options.feedback: Yes. *Me alegra que* expresses a feeling about someone else's action, so the subjunctive follows.

options.label: vienes
options.feedback: Not yet — even though it's a fact, a reaction like *me alegra que* takes the subjunctive.

options.label: venir
options.feedback: Not yet — the infinitive only works when the same person feels and acts (*me alegra venir*).

hints: Does the main clause assert a fact, or react to it?
After emotions + a different subject, use *que* + subjunctive.
exercises.solution: *Me alegra que* expresses an emotion, and the person coming (*tú*) is different from the person who's glad (*yo*). So the verb goes in the present subjunctive: *venir → vengo → **vengas***. *Me alegra mucho que vengas a la boda.*

options.label: tiene
options.feedback: Yes. *Creo que* asserts what you believe, so the indicative follows.

options.label: tenga
options.feedback: Not yet — *creer que* in the affirmative asserts a belief and takes the indicative. *No creo que* would take *tenga*.

options.label: tener
options.feedback: Not yet — after *creo que* you need a conjugated verb.

hints: Is the speaker asserting or doubting?
Affirmative *creer que* → indicative; negative *no creer que* → subjunctive.
exercises.solution: *Creer que* in the affirmative presents what follows as true (in the speaker's opinion), so it takes the **indicative**: *Creo que Marta **tiene** razón.* In the negative it flips: *No creo que Marta **tenga** razón.*

exercises.prompt: Fill the gap with the right form of *llover*: *No creo que ___ mañana.*
hints: *No creo que* expresses doubt. Which mood follows?
*Llover* is stem-changing (*o → ue*): *llueve* in the indicative.
exercises.solution: *No creo que* denies or doubts, so the verb goes in the **subjunctive**. *Llover* is an *-er* stem-changing verb (*llueve*), and in the subjunctive its ending takes *a*: **llueva**. *No creo que llueva mañana.*

feedback.message: Not yet — *llueve* is the indicative. After *no creo que*, use the subjunctive: *llueva*.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gap with the right form of *estar*: *Siento que tu abuela ___ enferma.*
hints: *Siento que* = I'm sorry that. Is it a feeling?
*Estar* is irregular in the subjunctive and carries a written accent.
exercises.solution: *Sentir que* (to be sorry that) expresses a feeling, so it takes the **subjunctive**. *Estar* is one of the six irregulars: *esté, estés, **esté**…* So: *Siento que tu abuela **esté** enferma.* Don't forget the accent: *este* without it means "this".

feedback.message: Almost — *esté* needs its accent on the last *e*.
Not yet — that's the indicative. After *siento que*, use the subjunctive: *esté*.

exercises.prompt: Make the sentence negative by starting with *No creo que*: *Creo que el museo abre los lunes.* → *No creo que el museo ___ los lunes.*
hints: Negating *creer que* changes the mood of the second verb.
*Abrir* is an *-ir* verb: its subjunctive endings have *a*.
exercises.solution: Negating *creo que* turns an assertion into doubt, so the second verb changes from the indicative to the **subjunctive**. *Abrir* → *abro* → *abr-* + *-a* = **abra**. *No creo que el museo abra los lunes.*

feedback.message: Not yet — after *no creo que*, the verb switches to the subjunctive: *abra*.

exercises.prompt: Translate using *ojalá*: *I hope it doesn't rain.*
hints: *Ojalá* is always followed by the subjunctive.
The subjunctive of *llover* is *llueva*. *Que* after *ojalá* is optional.
exercises.solution: *Ojalá* introduces a wish and always takes the **subjunctive**. *Llover* → *llueva*. So: ***Ojalá no llueva.*** You can also add *que*: *Ojalá que no llueva*. Both are correct and common.

feedback.message: Almost — *ojalá* has an accent on the last *a*.

exercises.prompt: Complete: *A lo mejor Lucía ___ a la fiesta esta noche.* (venir)

options.label: viene
options.feedback: Yes. *A lo mejor* is followed by the indicative.

options.label: venga
options.feedback: Not yet — *a lo mejor* takes the indicative. With *quizás* or *tal vez* the subjunctive would be possible.

options.label: vendría
options.feedback: Not yet — the conditional doesn't fit here; *a lo mejor* + present indicative is the natural choice.

hints: Of the words for "perhaps", one always takes the indicative.
*A lo mejor* behaves differently from *quizás* and *tal vez*.
exercises.solution: *A lo mejor* (maybe) is informal and always takes the **indicative**: *A lo mejor Lucía **viene** a la fiesta esta noche.* If you want to sound more doubtful, switch to *quizás* or *tal vez* with the subjunctive: *Quizás venga*.

exercises.prompt: Which of these are correct Spanish? Choose all that apply.

options.label: Tal vez viene mañana.
options.feedback: Yes. With *tal vez*, the indicative is correct and sounds like a reasonable guess.

options.label: Tal vez venga mañana.
options.feedback: Yes. With *tal vez*, the subjunctive is also correct and adds a little more doubt.

options.label: Puede que viene mañana.
options.feedback: Not yet — *puede que* always takes the subjunctive: *puede que venga*.

options.label: Es posible que venga mañana.
options.feedback: Yes. *Es posible que* always takes the subjunctive.

hints: Some "perhaps" words accept both moods; others only one.
*Puede que* and *es posible que* behave alike.
exercises.solution: **a** and **b** are both correct: *tal vez* (like *quizás*) takes either mood, the subjunctive sounding more doubtful. **d** is correct: *es posible que* always takes the subjunctive. **c** is not: *puede que* must be followed by the subjunctive, *puede que **venga** mañana*.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gap with the right form of *poner*: *Me molesta que mis vecinos ___ la música tan alta.*
hints: *Me molesta que* expresses a feeling. Which mood follows?
The *yo* form of *poner* is *pongo*.
exercises.solution: *Me molesta que* (it bothers me that) expresses a reaction, so it takes the **subjunctive**. *Poner* → *pongo* → *pong-* + *-an* (*ellos*) = **pongan**. *Me molesta que mis vecinos pongan la música tan alta.*

feedback.message: Not yet — after *me molesta que* the verb goes into the subjunctive: *pongan*.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gap with the right form of *poder*: *Dudo que nosotros ___ terminar el proyecto hoy.*
hints: *Dudo que* expresses doubt.
*Poder* is a stem-changer (*puedo*), but what happens in the *nosotros* form?
exercises.solution: *Dudo que* takes the **subjunctive**. *Poder* is an *-er* stem-changing verb: *pueda, puedas, pueda*, but *nosotros* and *vosotros* keep the original stem, as in the present indicative: **podamos**, *podáis*. *Dudo que podamos terminar el proyecto hoy.*

feedback.message: Not yet — that's the indicative. After *dudo que*, use the subjunctive: *podamos*.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Spanish, speaking to a friend (*tú*): *I'm glad you're here.*
answers: me alegra que tú estés aquí
me alegro de que tú estés aquí
me alegro de que estés aquí
estoy contento de que tú estés aquí
estoy contento de que estés aquí
estoy contenta de que tú estés aquí
estoy contenta de que estés aquí
me alegra que tú estés acá
me alegro de que tú estés acá
me alegro de que estés acá
hints: Use *me alegra que* or *me alegro de que*.
"You're here" is a fact, but after an emotion it still takes the subjunctive of *estar*.
exercises.solution: Two equally good ways to say "I'm glad": *me alegra que* (built like *gustar*) or *me alegro de que* (reflexive *alegrarse de*). Either way, the emotion triggers the **subjunctive**, so *estás* becomes *estés*: ***Me alegra que estés aquí*** or ***Me alegro de que estés aquí***. *Estoy contento/contenta de que estés aquí* also works.

feedback.message: Almost — after an emotion, use the subjunctive: *estés*.
Very close, and common in speech — but with *alegrarse*, careful Spanish keeps the *de*: *me alegro de que estés aquí*. Or say *me alegra que estés aquí*.
